# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value

native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain

producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`

import YulangClosure.HigherOrderSyntax

/-! Candidate immutable value-graph theory. Independent research syntax, NOT a
native heap model. `roll` below is an identity-typed transparent marker, not the
paper's iso-recursive introduction. The full paper parent remains open. -/
namespace YulangClosure.GuardedValueGraph

inductive Ty where
  | unit | bottom
  | product (left right : Ty)
  | arrow (argument result : Ty)
  | thunk (result : Ty)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- Bodies have explicit graph references and variables. No evaluation assumption. -/
inductive Term (R V : Type) where
  | ref (reference : R)
  | var (index : V)
  | unit
  | app (function argument : Term R V)
  | force (thunk : Term R V)

def Term.subst (fr : R → Term S W) (fv : V → Term S W) : Term R V → Term S W
  | .ref r => fr r
  | .var v => fv v
  | .unit => .unit
  | .app f a => .app (f.subst fr fv) (a.subst fr fv)
  | .force t => .force (t.subst fr fv)

inductive Typed (xi : R → Ty) (gamma : V → Ty) : Term R V → Ty → Prop where
  | ref (r) : Typed xi gamma (.ref r) (xi r)
  | var (v) : Typed xi gamma (.var v) (gamma v)
  | unit : Typed xi gamma .unit .unit
  | app : Typed xi gamma f (.arrow a b) → Typed xi gamma x a →
      Typed xi gamma (.app f x) b
  | force : Typed xi gamma t (.thunk a) → Typed xi gamma (.force t) a

theorem typed_subst {xi : R → Ty} {gamma : V → Ty}
    {yi : S → Ty} {delta : W → Ty} {t : Term R V} {a : Ty}
    (h : Typed xi gamma t a) (fr : R → Term S W) (fv : V → Term S W)
    (hr : ∀ r, Typed yi delta (fr r) (xi r))
    (hv : ∀ v, Typed yi delta (fv v) (gamma v)) :
    Typed yi delta (t.subst fr fv) a := by
  induction h with
  | ref r => exact hr r
  | var v => exact hv v
  | unit => exact .unit
  | app _ _ ihf iha => exact .app ihf iha
  | force _ ih => exact .force ih

def emptyTy : Empty → Ty := Empty.elim

def argTy (a : Ty) : Option Empty → Ty
  | none => a
  | some e => Empty.elim e

inductive Node (R : Type) where
  | unit
  | pair (left right : R)
  | lam (argument result : Ty) (body : Term R (Option Empty))
  | delay (result : Ty) (body : Term R Empty)
  | alias (target : R)
  | view (metadata : Nat) (target : R)
  | roll (target : R)
  | evidence (metadata : Nat) (target : R)

/-- Exactly the transparent edge; data fields and code references are guards. -/
def Node.next : Node R → Option R
  | .alias r | .view _ r | .roll r | .evidence _ r => some r
  | _ => none

def Node.map (f : R → S) : Node R → Node S
  | .unit => .unit
  | .pair l r => .pair (f l) (f r)
  | .lam a b body => .lam a b (body.subst (fun r => .ref (f r)) .var)
  | .delay a body => .delay a (body.subst (fun r => .ref (f r)) .var)
  | .alias r => .alias (f r)
  | .view m r => .view m (f r)
  | .roll r => .roll (f r)
  | .evidence m r => .evidence m (f r)

theorem next_map (f : R → S) (n : Node R) :
    (n.map f).next = n.next.map f := by cases n <;> rfl

inductive NodeTyped (xi : R → Ty) : Node R → Ty → Prop where
  | unit : NodeTyped xi .unit .unit
  | pair (l r) : NodeTyped xi (.pair l r) (.product (xi l) (xi r))
  | lam : Typed xi (argTy a) body b → NodeTyped xi (.lam a b body) (.arrow a b)
  | delay : Typed xi emptyTy body a → NodeTyped xi (.delay a body) (.thunk a)
  | alias (r) : NodeTyped xi (.alias r) (xi r)
  | view (m r) : NodeTyped xi (.view m r) (xi r)
  | roll (r) : NodeTyped xi (.roll r) (xi r)
  | evidence (m r) : NodeTyped xi (.evidence m r) (xi r)

theorem node_map {xi : R → Ty} {yi : S → Ty} {n : Node R} {a : Ty}
    (f : R → S) (hf : ∀ r, yi (f r) = xi r) (h : NodeTyped xi n a) :
    NodeTyped yi (n.map f) a := by
  induction h with
  | unit => exact .unit
  | pair l r => simpa only [Node.map, hf] using NodeTyped.pair (xi := yi) (f l) (f r)
  | lam hb =>
      apply NodeTyped.lam
      exact typed_subst hb _ _ (fun r => by simpa only [hf] using Typed.ref (xi := yi) (gamma := argTy _) (f r)) (fun v => .var v)
  | delay hb =>
      apply NodeTyped.delay
      exact typed_subst hb _ _ (fun r => by simpa only [hf] using Typed.ref (xi := yi) (gamma := emptyTy) (f r)) (fun v => .var v)
  | alias r => simpa only [Node.map, hf] using NodeTyped.alias (xi := yi) (f r)
  | view m r => simpa only [Node.map, hf] using NodeTyped.view (xi := yi) m (f r)
  | roll r => simpa only [Node.map, hf] using NodeTyped.roll (xi := yi) (f r)
  | evidence m r => simpa only [Node.map, hf] using NodeTyped.evidence (xi := yi) m (f r)

abbrev Graph (R : Type) := R → Node R
abbrev FiniteGraph (size : Nat) := Graph (Fin size)
def WellTyped (g : Graph R) (xi : R → Ty) : Prop := ∀ r, NodeTyped xi (g r) (xi r)

/-- A finite numeric certificate for transparent edges only. `bound` enables
allocation into a larger graph without computing a maximum or using choice. -/
structure Guarded (g : Graph R) where
  rank : R → Nat
  ceiling : Nat
  bound : ∀ r, rank r < ceiling
  decrease : ∀ r s, (g r).next = some s → rank s < rank r

inductive Observes (g : Graph R) : R → Node R → Prop where
  | done (r) : (g r).next = none → Observes g r (g r)
  | step : (g r).next = some s → Observes g s n → Observes g r n

theorem finite_observation (g : Graph R) (guard : Guarded g) (r : R) :
    ∃ n, Observes g r n := by
  have aux : ∀ k r, guard.rank r < k → ∃ n, Observes g r n := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => intro r h; exact False.elim (Nat.not_lt_zero _ h)
    | succ k ih =>
        intro r h
        cases hn : (g r).next with
        | none => exact ⟨g r, .done r hn⟩
        | some s =>
            have hs : guard.rank s < k := Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le
              (guard.decrease r s hn) (Nat.le_of_lt_succ h)
            obtain ⟨n, ho⟩ := ih s hs
            exact ⟨n, .step hn ho⟩
  exact aux (guard.rank r + 1) r (Nat.lt_succ_self _)

theorem transparent_type {xi : R → Ty} {n : Node R} {a : Ty}
    (h : NodeTyped xi n a) (hn : n.next = some s) : xi s = a := by
  cases h with
  | unit => cases hn
  | pair l r => cases hn
  | lam hb => cases hn
  | delay hb => cases hn
  | alias r => cases hn; rfl
  | view m r => cases hn; rfl
  | roll r => cases hn; rfl
  | evidence m r => cases hn; rfl

theorem observation_typed {g : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty} (hg : WellTyped g xi)
    {r : R} {n : Node R} (h : Observes g r n) :
    NodeTyped xi n (xi r) ∧ n.next = none := by
  induction h with
  | done r hn => exact ⟨hg r, hn⟩
  | @step r s n hs ho ih =>
      have he := transparent_type (hg r) hs
      exact ⟨he ▸ ih.1, ih.2⟩

/-- Canonical terminal nodes, derived by inversion of concrete node typing. -/
inductive Canonical : Ty → Node R → Prop where
  | unit : Canonical .unit .unit
  | pair (l r) : Canonical (.product a b) (.pair l r)
  | lam (body) : Canonical (.arrow a b) (.lam a b body)
  | delay (body) : Canonical (.thunk a) (.delay a body)

theorem terminal_canonical {xi : R → Ty} {n : Node R} {a : Ty}
    (h : NodeTyped xi n a) (hn : n.next = none) : Canonical a n := by
  cases h with
  | unit => exact .unit
  | pair l r => exact .pair l r
  | lam hb => exact .lam _
  | delay hb => exact .delay _
  | alias r => cases hn
  | view m r => cases hn
  | roll r => cases hn
  | evidence m r => cases hn

theorem reference_canonical {g : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (guard : Guarded g) (r : R) :
    ∃ n, Observes g r n ∧ Canonical (xi r) n := by
  obtain ⟨n, ho⟩ := finite_observation g guard r
  obtain ⟨ht, hn⟩ := observation_typed hg ho
  exact ⟨n, ho, terminal_canonical ht hn⟩

theorem no_bottom_reference {g : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (guard : Guarded g) (r : R) : xi r ≠ .bottom := by
  intro hb
  obtain ⟨n, _, hc⟩ := reference_canonical hg guard r
  rw [hb] at hc
  cases hc

/-- Nonempty paths in the transparent subgraph, not in the whole graph. -/
inductive TransparentPath (g : Graph R) : R → R → Prop where
  | edge : (g r).next = some s → TransparentPath g r s
  | cons : (g r).next = some s → TransparentPath g s t → TransparentPath g r t

theorem transparent_path_rank {g : Graph R} (guard : Guarded g)
    {r s : R} (h : TransparentPath g r s) : guard.rank s < guard.rank r := by
  induction h with
  | edge h => exact guard.decrease _ _ h
  | cons h _ ih => exact Nat.lt_trans ih (guard.decrease _ _ h)

theorem no_transparent_cycle {g : Graph R} (guard : Guarded g) (r : R) :
    TransparentPath g r r → False := by
  intro h
  exact Nat.lt_irrefl _ (transparent_path_rank guard h)

theorem no_transparent_self {g : Graph R} (guard : Guarded g) (r : R) :
    (g r).next ≠ some r := by
  intro h
  exact Nat.lt_irrefl _ (guard.decrease r r h)

theorem no_transparent_two_cycle {g : Graph R} (guard : Guarded g) (r s : R)
    (h : (g r).next = some s) : (g s).next ≠ some r := by
  intro h'
  exact Nat.lt_irrefl _ (Nat.lt_trans (guard.decrease r s h) (guard.decrease s r h'))

/-- Simultaneous allocation uses disjoint constructors, so all new names exist
before typing their bodies and no new reference can collide with an old one. -/
def joinTy (xi : R → Ty) (nu : S → Ty) : Sum R S → Ty
  | .inl r => xi r
  | .inr s => nu s

def allocate (g : Graph R) (fresh : S → Node (Sum R S)) : Graph (Sum R S)
  | .inl r => (g r).map Sum.inl
  | .inr s => fresh s

theorem allocation_old_node (g : Graph R) (fresh : S → Node (Sum R S)) (r : R) :
    allocate g fresh (.inl r) = (g r).map Sum.inl := rfl

/-- Old observations are preserved by the injective reference renaming. -/
theorem allocation_observation {g : Graph R} (fresh : S → Node (Sum R S))
    {r : R} {n : Node R} (h : Observes g r n) :
    Observes (allocate g fresh) (.inl r) (n.map Sum.inl) := by
  induction h with
  | done r hn =>
      apply Observes.done
      simp only [allocate, next_map, hn, Option.map_none]
  | @step r s n hs _ ih =>
      apply Observes.step (s := Sum.inl s)
      · simp only [allocate, next_map, hs, Option.map_some]
      · exact ih

theorem allocation_old_type (xi : R → Ty) (nu : S → Ty) (r : R) :
    joinTy xi nu (.inl r) = xi r := rfl

theorem fresh_no_collision (r : R) (s : S) :
    (Sum.inl r : Sum R S) ≠ Sum.inr s := by intro h; cases h

theorem allocate_typed {g : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty} {nu : S → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (fresh : S → Node (Sum R S))
    (hf : ∀ s, NodeTyped (joinTy xi nu) (fresh s) (nu s)) :
    WellTyped (allocate g fresh) (joinTy xi nu) := by
  intro r
  cases r with
  | inl r => exact node_map Sum.inl (fun _ => rfl) (hg r)
  | inr s => exact hf s

/-- New-to-old transparent edges are harmless. Only new-to-new transparent
edges need the local rec guard check. Old nodes never acquire edges to new nodes. -/
def allocate_guard {g : Graph R} (guard : Guarded g)
    (fresh : S → Node (Sum R S)) (rank : S → Nat) (ceiling : Nat)
    (bound : ∀ s, rank s < ceiling)
    (decrease : ∀ s t, (fresh s).next = some (.inr t) → rank t < rank s) :
    Guarded (allocate g fresh) where
  rank := fun r => match r with
    | .inl r => guard.rank r
    | .inr s => guard.ceiling + rank s
  ceiling := guard.ceiling + ceiling
  bound := by
    intro r
    cases r with
    | inl r => exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (guard.bound r) (Nat.le_add_right _ _)
    | inr s => exact Nat.add_lt_add_left (bound s) _
  decrease := by
    intro r t h
    cases r with
    | inl r =>
        change ((g r).map Sum.inl).next = some t at h
        rw [next_map] at h
        cases hn : (g r).next with
        | none => simp [hn] at h
        | some s =>
            simp only [hn, Option.map_some] at h
            cases h
            exact guard.decrease r s hn
    | inr s =>
        change (fresh s).next = some t at h
        cases t with
        | inl r => exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (guard.bound r) (Nat.le_add_right _ _)
        | inr t => exact Nat.add_lt_add_left (decrease s t h) _

/-- The rec body is closed by simultaneous replacement of every recursive
variable by its allocated reference. Mutual dependencies do not require an order. -/
def closeBody (body : Term R S) : Term (Sum R S) Empty :=
  body.subst (fun r => .ref (.inl r)) (fun s => .ref (.inr s))

theorem closeBody_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : S → Ty} {body : Term R S} {a : Ty}
    (h : Typed xi nu body a) : Typed (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy (closeBody body) a :=
  typed_subst (yi := joinTy xi nu) (delta := emptyTy) h _ _
    (fun r => Typed.ref (Sum.inl r)) (fun s => Typed.ref (Sum.inr s))

theorem old_body_weakening {xi : R → Ty} (nu : S → Ty) {gamma : V → Ty}
    {body : Term R V} {a : Ty} (h : Typed xi gamma body a) :
    Typed (joinTy xi nu) gamma (body.subst (fun r => .ref (.inl r)) .var) a :=
  typed_subst (yi := joinTy xi nu) (delta := gamma) h _ _
    (fun r => Typed.ref (Sum.inl r)) (fun v => Typed.var v)

/-- The conjunction applies allocation lemmas to the parent graph-extension
obligation for this syntax; typing and the local guard are separate premises. -/
theorem rec_extension {g : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty} {nu : S → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (guard : Guarded g)
    (fresh : S → Node (Sum R S))
    (hf : ∀ s, NodeTyped (joinTy xi nu) (fresh s) (nu s))
    (rank : S → Nat) (ceiling : Nat) (bound : ∀ s, rank s < ceiling)
    (decrease : ∀ s t, (fresh s).next = some (.inr t) → rank t < rank s)
    {body : Term R S} {a : Ty} (hb : Typed xi nu body a) :
    WellTyped (allocate g fresh) (joinTy xi nu) ∧
    (∀ r, ∃ n, Observes (allocate g fresh) r n ∧ Canonical (joinTy xi nu r) n) ∧
    Typed (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy (closeBody body) a := by
  have ht := allocate_typed hg fresh hf
  have hg' := allocate_guard guard fresh rank ceiling bound decrease
  exact ⟨ht, reference_canonical ht hg', closeBody_typed hb⟩

/-- Genuine mutual lambda recursion: each body calls the other node. -/
def mutualLambda : Graph Bool
  | false => .lam .unit .unit (.app (.ref true) (.var none))
  | true => .lam .unit .unit (.app (.ref false) (.var none))

def mutualLambdaTy : Bool → Ty := fun _ => .arrow .unit .unit

theorem mutualLambda_typed : WellTyped mutualLambda mutualLambdaTy := by
  intro r
  cases r <;> exact NodeTyped.lam (Typed.app (Typed.ref _) (Typed.var none))

def mutualLambda_guard : Guarded mutualLambda where
  rank := fun _ => 0
  ceiling := 1
  bound := fun _ => Nat.zero_lt_succ _
  decrease := by intro r s h; cases r <;> cases h

/-- Shared child references are allowed, independently of whether their ranks
are lower: a pair node is a genuine constructor guard. -/
def sharedPair : Graph Bool
  | false => .unit
  | true => .pair false false

def sharedPairTy : Bool → Ty
  | false => .unit
  | true => .product .unit .unit

theorem sharedPair_typed : WellTyped sharedPair sharedPairTy := by
  intro r
  cases r
  · exact .unit
  · exact .pair false false

def sharedPair_guard : Guarded sharedPair where
  rank := fun _ => 0
  ceiling := 1
  bound := fun _ => Nat.zero_lt_succ _
  decrease := by intro r s h; cases r <;> cases h

/-- Typing alone permits a bogus bottom cycle. The guard certificate rejects it. -/
def transparentCycle : Graph Bool
  | false => .view 7 true
  | true => .roll false

theorem transparentCycle_typed_bottom : WellTyped transparentCycle (fun _ => .bottom) := by
  intro r
  cases r
  · exact .view 7 true
  · exact .roll false

theorem transparentCycle_unguarded : Guarded transparentCycle → False := by
  intro guard
  exact no_transparent_two_cycle guard false true rfl rfl

def emptyGraph : Graph Empty := Empty.elim

def emptyGuard : Guarded emptyGraph where
  rank := Empty.elim
  ceiling := 0
  bound := by intro r; cases r
  decrease := fun r => Empty.elim r

theorem emptyGraph_typed : WellTyped emptyGraph emptyTy := by intro r; cases r

/-- An actual allocation of both mutually recursive functions at once. -/
def mutualFresh (b : Bool) : Node (Sum Empty Bool) := (mutualLambda b).map Sum.inr

def allocatedMutual : Graph (Sum Empty Bool) := allocate emptyGraph mutualFresh

theorem mutualFresh_typed (b : Bool) :
    NodeTyped (joinTy emptyTy mutualLambdaTy) (mutualFresh b) (mutualLambdaTy b) :=
  node_map Sum.inr (fun _ => rfl) (mutualLambda_typed b)

theorem allocatedMutual_typed :
    WellTyped allocatedMutual (joinTy emptyTy mutualLambdaTy) :=
  allocate_typed emptyGraph_typed mutualFresh mutualFresh_typed

def allocatedMutual_guard : Guarded allocatedMutual :=
  allocate_guard emptyGuard mutualFresh (fun _ => 0) 1
    (fun _ => Nat.zero_lt_succ _) (by intro s t h; cases s <;> cases h)

theorem allocatedMutual_observes (b : Bool) :
    ∃ n, Observes allocatedMutual (.inr b) n ∧ Canonical (.arrow .unit .unit) n :=
  reference_canonical allocatedMutual_typed allocatedMutual_guard (.inr b)

/-- Freshness and per-node typing do not suffice: a fresh self-alias is rejected. -/
def badFresh (_ : Unit) : Node (Sum Empty Unit) := .alias (.inr ())

theorem badFresh_typed (u : Unit) :
    NodeTyped (joinTy emptyTy (fun _ : Unit => Ty.bottom)) (badFresh u) .bottom :=
  NodeTyped.alias (xi := joinTy emptyTy (fun _ : Unit => Ty.bottom)) (Sum.inr ())

theorem badAllocation_typed :
    WellTyped (allocate emptyGraph badFresh) (joinTy emptyTy (fun _ : Unit => Ty.bottom)) :=
  allocate_typed emptyGraph_typed badFresh badFresh_typed

theorem badAllocation_unguarded : Guarded (allocate emptyGraph badFresh) → False := by
  intro guard
  exact no_transparent_self guard (.inr ()) rfl

end YulangClosure.GuardedValueGraph

# Guarded immutable value graphs: candidate theory

Status: primary Lean checks passed for the candidate; fresh independent review pending.
Author: `/root/guarded_value_graph_astra_r1`; requested gpt-6-astra/medium;
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. No descendants. Original author freeze had no coauthor; primary is a coauthor of subsequent elaboration repairs.
Authority: PARALLEL-THEORY-20261025/r1, SHA-256
`0751276e8eedf50d113475a0ef1c41b27b7ffd77cc4ccc28761e3cc9e792ff76`.
This is an implementation-independent research model, with no production authority.

## Parent and exact represented domain

The parent is ENV-GRAPH-1 and the immutable graph-extension/value-forms claims in
`docs/yulang-operational-type-safety-ja.tex`, lines 150–196, 258–267, 980–1010.
The paper requires finite immutable reference graphs, cycles guarded by genuine
data/lambda/delay constructors, finite outer-constructor observation, simultaneous
rec allocation preserving old typing, canonical elimination forms and absence of
closed bottom values. ENV-GRAPH-1 also requires native recursive/shared graph
readback, including preallocated uninitialized cells. That native part remains OPEN.

`GuardedValueGraph.lean` deliberately names a separate namespace and syntax. Its
types are unit, bottom, binary product, arrow and thunk. Concrete graph nodes are
unit, pair, lambda with body, delay with body, alias, metadata-bearing view,
roll marker and metadata-bearing evidence. Bodies contain references, variables,
unit, application and force. Lambda bodies have one explicit argument slot;
delay bodies have none. Node fields and bodies store references, so graph
recursion is actual reference recursion, not recursive meta-level Lean objects.
`FiniteGraph n` uses `Fin n`; allocating m names gives the finite disjoint domain
`Sum (Fin n) (Fin m)`. General helper lemmas also work for arbitrary reference
sorts equipped with the same bounded rank certificate.

**This is not the complete paper grammar or an embedding of HigherOrderSyntax.**
The accepted HigherOrderSyntax import supplies the existing library environment;
no theorem or syntactic identification with its values is assumed. In particular:

- `roll` is an identity-typed transparent marker. There is no μ type and no proof
  that a real roll/unroll pair changes between μA and its unfolded body correctly.
- Views and evidence preserve the identical type. Metadata is retained as a Nat,
  with no interpretation theorem. Type-changing evidence, type abstraction and
  application, polymorphism, union/intersection/top introductions are absent.
- Pairs represent one genuine data form. Records, required/optional fields,
  sequences, nominal tags and arities, arbitrary literals, continuations and
  handlers are absent.
- Lambda entry modes, receipts, adapters, result consumers, wrappers, dynamic
  Call's delayed carrier protocol, request binders and full computation syntax
  are absent. The body substitution theorem covers the explicitly given Term
  grammar, not the accepted core's mutual Value/Comp/Adapter grammar.

These omissions keep the original parents OPEN; they do not narrow their claims.

## Concrete guard and finite observation

`Node.next` returns exactly the target of alias/view/roll/evidence and returns
none for unit/pair/lambda/delay. A `Guarded g` certificate consists of numeric
ranks, a finite ceiling and the local inequalities rank(s) < rank(r) for every
transparent edge r→s. There is no decrease condition on pair fields or references
inside lambda/delay bodies. This is a local arithmetic condition on actual node
constructors, not a supplied observation theorem or assumed canonical form.

`finite_observation` inducts on a strict upper bound for the starting rank. A
transparent edge decreases that bound; a node with no transparent edge ends the
observation. `TransparentPath` and `transparent_path_rank` reject every nonempty
transparent cycle. Thus the whole graph may have cycles, provided no cycle is
entirely transparent. The rank certificate is sufficient for the paper's desired
finite observation, but **rank existence from the paper's syntactic cycle
condition is not proved**. A finite transparent-subgraph topological ranking or a
complete guard checker remains GVG-GUARD-COMPLETE-1. No graph-wide DAG hypothesis
is used or proposed as a language restriction.

`transparent_type` derives preservation of the exact type along each transparent
edge by node-typing inversion. `observation_typed` transports typing through the
finite observation. `terminal_canonical` then inverts only actual terminal
constructors. `reference_canonical` combines these results. `no_bottom_reference`
follows because no terminal constructor introduces bottom. It does not claim
that computations cannot have bottom type or that recursive computation terminates.

## Allocation and application to the parent

`allocate g fresh` injects old names with `Sum.inl` and fresh names with `Sum.inr`.
It maps references inside old nodes without changing their content; the old
subgraph gains no edge to a fresh node. `joinTy` preserves every old assignment
exactly. `fresh_no_collision` derives disjointness of old and new names.
`node_map`, `allocation_old_node`, `allocation_old_type` and
`allocation_observation` provide typing/content/observation preservation under
this explicit renaming. No mutable cell update is modeled.

All fresh names are available simultaneously to all fresh nodes. `allocate_typed`
requires individual fresh-node derivations against the joined assignment and
constructs the whole resulting graph typing. It does not assume post-graph
welltypedness. Lambda body typing checks its actual Term, and delay body typing
likewise checks the body. The arbitrary-node premise is still a premise: no
claim is made that paper/source rec constructors already supply those derivations.

`allocate_guard` constructs the post-graph ranks. Old rank stays rank_old; fresh
rank becomes ceiling_old + rank_fresh. An old edge stays old. A fresh-to-old
edge decreases because every old rank is below ceiling_old. A fresh-to-fresh
transparent edge decreases by the local rec rank check. The resulting ceiling is
ceiling_old + ceiling_fresh. Thus the post-graph guard is derived rather than
assumed, and mutually referring fresh guarded nodes need no allocation order.

`typed_subst` proves simultaneous replacement of reference and variable leaves
by typed Terms by induction on the body typing. `closeBody_typed` replaces all
recursive variables by fresh references in one substitution;
`old_body_weakening` preserves old derivations under the joined assignment.
`rec_extension` consumes all these lemmas and returns post-graph typing, finite
typed canonical observation at every old/new reference, and the typed closed
rec body. This discharges the corresponding restricted research-model implication
in the primary-checked construction; it is a concrete application to the parent proof
step, not closure of the paper or native ENV-GRAPH-1 claim.

## Distinguishing constructions and falsifiers

- `mutualLambda` has two lambdas whose bodies call one another. Both ranks are
  zero. `allocatedMutual` allocates them simultaneously into an empty old graph;
  per-node typing, the combined guard and observations are constructed.
- `sharedPair` has two fields pointing to the same unit node, also with equal
  zero ranks. Sharing and guarded edges are not rejected by a DAG requirement.
- `transparentCycle` consists of a view edge and a roll edge back to its start.
  It has a node-typing assignment with bottom everywhere but has no Guarded
  certificate. Hence graph node typing alone cannot justify bottom exclusion.
- `badFresh` allocates a fresh self-alias with bottom typing. Freshness and every
  individual new-node typing premise hold; `badAllocation_unguarded` rejects the
  resulting graph. The local new transparent-edge guard is essential.
- `no_transparent_self` rejects alias, view, roll or evidence self-loops uniformly;
  `no_transparent_two_cycle` and `no_transparent_cycle` cover mixed/longer loops.
- Replacing an old node's type is excluded by `allocation_old_type`; allocating a
  new name equal to an old one contradicts `fresh_no_collision`.

These are theorem constructions in the candidate, not executed tests and not
observations of actual compiler constructors.

## Remaining owners and mutual TODOs

GVG-CHECK-1 — primary: elaborate the frozen Lean file, inspect its theorem/axiom
boundary, repair only after author STOP, and obtain independent review. Falsifier:
any elaboration failure, admitted proof, forbidden axiom, or quantified conclusion
that fails for the represented constructor domain.

GVG-GUARD-COMPLETE-1 — next graph proof allocation: construct a bounded rank from
an explicit finite graph with no all-transparent directed cycle. Falsifier: a
finite cycle-guarded graph for which the proposed construction fails to assign a
strictly decreasing transparent rank. This direction is currently OPEN.

GVG-FORMS-1 — next full-paper graph proof allocation: add the actual missing
constructors and type-changing roll/view/type-evidence rules, then establish the
correct elimination-specific typed observations. Falsifier: a well-typed guarded
μ/view/type-application graph for which transparent traversal changes the type
without preserving the eliminator evidence. Keep this separate from the local
identity-typed `transparent_type` lemma.

GVG-REC-RHS-1 — full paper syntax owner: derive fresh-node typing from the original
rec RHS derivations under simultaneous binder-aware substitution, including all
lambda/adapter/request binders. Current node_map and Term substitution are usable
sublemmas only in their stated domain. Falsifier: capture or a missing recursive
reference in any represented full-paper RHS constructor.

ENV-GRAPH-1 — Luna/source intake: graph readback and original typing from actual
machine local/global initialization, current cells, Lambda/Callee/ValueEntry and
lookup/extend owners, including preallocation and uninitialized states. This
assignment performs no native audit and makes no native correspondence claim.
The existing constructor-map and native-environment notes are used only to retain
that obligation and ownership, not as evidence of graph realization. No production
implementation TODO is authorized or needed by this independent theory packet.

All original Simple-sub generation, accumulation, propagation, levels, extrusion,
intrusion, generalization and F1/FK1/foreign-continuation quantifiers remain
unchanged and OPEN outside their independently established premises.

## Frozen evidence and resources

Lean artifact SHA-256:
`4d2c3b17d0ab8d12606c875638426167ce596492167cecf042eb222436229f55`.
Paper dependency: `a003b56a2f32eed06a2c604ef8aed043d43752cbed0b09028eff7f6efac4886b`.
HigherOrderSyntax: `ea727d33692bdcbe6b40245b960d01225b556b5334ffab649eea2699930d5972`.
Higher-order design: `50eb7ebd2ed2d155dfeca2e3ce99f3f5b990cc4f1bf101663949a04d8d4b748f`.
Toolchain: `ca5f1f601d34c49079e38d7e7041eb0f2a9c227fbc1df0f404820069a052330c`.
Lakefile: `2514197994dc47b5e4c6f15ff8c9251f994056b6e32bf2648588ffc10251e194`.
Manifest: `058325944d936e85c1f601e68f3147f790dbbd0d0286357949466ce1ad3504c3`.

No historical proof is generalized beyond its premises; no historical failed
construction is revived. This file contains a new candidate construction.
No Lean/test/build/checker call was run by the author. Primary owns all checking.
Only the Lean file, this note and the assigned inbox are written. No scratch
paths, compiler/config edits, Git, network, descendants or background processes.
The assignment has a 600-second cap; exact dispatch time is UNKNOWN within the
primary's 06:36:20.860946Z–06:36:43.352751Z interval. The final inbox records freeze
time and conservative elapsed usage. Author stops writing at that freeze.

## Primary verification intake

Both authors stopped before primary takeover. Primary is a coauthor of elaboration repairs; all failed checker rows and original author handoffs remain intact. Safety repairs apply context induction hypotheses to the supplied typing derivation, type existential contexts explicitly, and use trace induction with generalized typing indices. Graph repairs rename a reserved binder, eliminate Empty dependently, expose the observed successor and give explicit joined reference types. No theorem premise or operational rule was weakened. Primary records final module/query hashes and axiom reports in `tasks/agent-loop/inbox/20261025-parallel-theory-r1-verification.jsonl`; fresh nonauthor review remains required. No compiler/native tests ran.

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a
failed proof check. Primary owns bounded elaboration, public signature/axiom
inspection, distinguishing examples, repairs after author STOP and fresh
independent review. Author/coauthor cannot independently certify this candidate.
Only the four exact leased files were created; there are no scratch paths,
background processes, descendants, compiler changes or Git operations.

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` research grammar. The stronger full-language/native
safety and original Simple-sub A/B obligations remain OPEN. This candidate
introduces an independent, explicitly defined research transition relation;
it does not infer operational adequacy from the structural embedding or from
successful typing of entry plans. The operational paper remains a proposal.

`Safety.preservation` quantifies over every context, computation, type, event and
raw `Step` derivation. No transition premise contains typing, preservation,
progress or body safety. `closed_progress` quantifies over every closed typing
derivation. `finite_prefix_safety` quantifies over every finite labelled trace,
including the empty trace; its endpoint retains the original type and is a
return, a concrete suspended request/failure, or has another transition.
Explicit failure is an admitted terminal outcome, not an excluded runtime error.
The theorem proves safety, not termination, successful completion, or absence
of explicit failures.

## Operational construction and parent application

Thunks, callable lambdas/wrappers, unions and intersections have recursive
canonical forms through any finite nest of views. A closed bottom value is
impossible. These lemmas are applied directly in closed progress. In particular,
a typed dynamic call cannot reach a literal/noncallable head, and a viewed thunk
has a specific Force transition rather than being omitted from the theorem.

The raw transition relation evaluates only the first computation of bind and
the bodies of scope/expose. It substitutes at bind/union selection, projects
single-child intersections, and enters callable lambda/wrap plans. Scope and
expose remain syntactically active around the executing computation, including
around a suspended operation. A return exits them with an event carrying their
exact annotations. No rules execute inside delay, lambda body, adapter body,
request continuation or the delayed wrap input before the appropriate entry.

Value-mode entry first forces the carrier and binds the returned value into the
body. Computation-mode entry substitutes the original carrier without forcing.
Both then bind the body result into the separate result consumer. A wrap delays
input adaptation inside the carrier passed to the inner call; its output adapter
runs only after the inner result. Definitional equations expose these orders.
Existing checked entry-plan typing and simultaneous substitution supply the
one-step typing proof. Preservation is then applied along each actual finite
trace, and progress is applied to the preserved endpoint. Neither arbitrary
body safety nor an assumed safe-transition supplier appears in these proofs.

`Suspended` is restricted to an explicit failure/request under the three actual
evaluation contexts. `suspended_decomposition` extracts the concrete terminal
node and finite context. Requests retain their operation instance, payload,
continuation and response binder; arbitrary stuck computations cannot become
terminal by definition. `returned_no_step` and `suspended_no_step` establish that
these states really lack an internal transition.

`context_inversion` and `plug_typed` supply the missing context argument for
resumption. `resume_in_context_typed` quantifies independently over every
retained context and every response value typed at the operation response type.
It substitutes the response into the actual request continuation and reinstalls
the entire context. Internal traces exclude external responses; this separate
lemma supplies typed resumption, not authenticity of externally received data.
It does not discharge F1/FK1 or arbitrary foreign native continuation claims.

## Metadata boundary: retention is not adequacy

Each observed view emits its exact `ViewOccurrence`. Lambda entry emits the
complete `LambdaEntryPlan`, including receipt, annotated types, body, consumer
and carrier. Wrap entry emits both complete adapters and the carrier. These
objects retain paths, views and proof-valued path correspondence. `Steps` keeps
all events in execution order. Original annotations are thus available in the
trace even when a computation projection uses `adapterBody`.

This is **syntactic historical retention only**. View observation advances to
the underlying eliminand and records the occurrence; it does not establish the
view's live propagation, licensing, receipt emission, provider ownership,
path mapping or owner discharge. The ledger model is an explicit candidate
semantics, not evidence that discarding those obligations in the real language
is valid. In particular the permissive `PathRule.adapterMap` and absent runtime
map identity remain untouched. Safety of this model cannot prove the paper's
full view/receipt semantics, source authenticity or compiler correctness.

The exact remaining adequacy premise is a relation between actual source/native
states and this annotated transition system that preserves active view/receipt/
owner behavior and covers every actual successor, request instance and response.
If ledger observations cannot represent that behavior, this operational model
needs a separately authorized semantic refinement before application. The full
parent must not be marked closed by the candidate's internal progress theorem.

## Coverage and falsifiers

Every Value/Comp/Adapter constructor of the accepted finite grammar is covered
by typing plus the progress proof. Literal payloads, top/injection/intersection
wrappers and nested callables are retained. Adapters enter through their actual
bodies using the frozen substitution/entry constructions. There is no recursion
primitive or immutable graph representation here; the independent graph lane
owns that separate extension, which is not imported.

The primary should check every declaration and its axiom list, then distinguish:
viewed Force; nested viewed callables; rejected literal application typing;
value versus computation entry; wrap input/output order and inert argument;
request response binder; consumer-after-body order; scope/expose around request;
and arbitrary typed response under an outer bind. Any missing typed constructor,
typing premise in `Step`, prematurely executed carrier/input adapter, missing
request/context field or unsupported metadata-adequacy claim falsifies the
corresponding result. No checker, build or test was run by this author.

# Guarded immutable value graphs: candidate theory

Status: primary Lean checks passed for the candidate; fresh independent review pending.
Author: `/root/guarded_value_graph_astra_r1`; requested gpt-6-astra/medium;
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. No descendants. Original author freeze had no coauthor; primary is a coauthor of subsequent elaboration repairs.
Authority: PARALLEL-THEORY-20261025/r1, SHA-256
`0751276e8eedf50d113475a0ef1c41b27b7ffd77cc4ccc28761e3cc9e792ff76`.
This is an implementation-independent research model, with no production authority.

## Parent and exact represented domain

The parent is ENV-GRAPH-1 and the immutable graph-extension/value-forms claims in
`docs/yulang-operational-type-safety-ja.tex`, lines 150–196, 258–267, 980–1010.
The paper requires finite immutable reference graphs, cycles guarded by genuine
data/lambda/delay constructors, finite outer-constructor observation, simultaneous
rec allocation preserving old typing, canonical elimination forms and absence of
closed bottom values. ENV-GRAPH-1 also requires native recursive/shared graph
readback, including preallocated uninitialized cells. That native part remains OPEN.

`GuardedValueGraph.lean` deliberately names a separate namespace and syntax. Its
types are unit, bottom, binary product, arrow and thunk. Concrete graph nodes are
unit, pair, lambda with body, delay with body, alias, metadata-bearing view,
roll marker and metadata-bearing evidence. Bodies contain references, variables,
unit, application and force. Lambda bodies have one explicit argument slot;
delay bodies have none. Node fields and bodies store references, so graph
recursion is actual reference recursion, not recursive meta-level Lean objects.
`FiniteGraph n` uses `Fin n`; allocating m names gives the finite disjoint domain
`Sum (Fin n) (Fin m)`. General helper lemmas also work for arbitrary reference
sorts equipped with the same bounded rank certificate.

**This is not the complete paper grammar or an embedding of HigherOrderSyntax.**
The accepted HigherOrderSyntax import supplies the existing library environment;
no theorem or syntactic identification with its values is assumed. In particular:

- `roll` is an identity-typed transparent marker. There is no μ type and no proof
  that a real roll/unroll pair changes between μA and its unfolded body correctly.
- Views and evidence preserve the identical type. Metadata is retained as a Nat,
  with no interpretation theorem. Type-changing evidence, type abstraction and
  application, polymorphism, union/intersection/top introductions are absent.
- Pairs represent one genuine data form. Records, required/optional fields,
  sequences, nominal tags and arities, arbitrary literals, continuations and
  handlers are absent.
- Lambda entry modes, receipts, adapters, result consumers, wrappers, dynamic
  Call's delayed carrier protocol, request binders and full computation syntax
  are absent. The body substitution theorem covers the explicitly given Term
  grammar, not the accepted core's mutual Value/Comp/Adapter grammar.

These omissions keep the original parents OPEN; they do not narrow their claims.

## Concrete guard and finite observation

`Node.next` returns exactly the target of alias/view/roll/evidence and returns
none for unit/pair/lambda/delay. A `Guarded g` certificate consists of numeric
ranks, a finite ceiling and the local inequalities rank(s) < rank(r) for every
transparent edge r→s. There is no decrease condition on pair fields or references
inside lambda/delay bodies. This is a local arithmetic condition on actual node
constructors, not a supplied observation theorem or assumed canonical form.

`finite_observation` inducts on a strict upper bound for the starting rank. A
transparent edge decreases that bound; a node with no transparent edge ends the
observation. `TransparentPath` and `transparent_path_rank` reject every nonempty
transparent cycle. Thus the whole graph may have cycles, provided no cycle is
entirely transparent. The rank certificate is sufficient for the paper's desired
finite observation, but **rank existence from the paper's syntactic cycle
condition is not proved**. A finite transparent-subgraph topological ranking or a
complete guard checker remains GVG-GUARD-COMPLETE-1. No graph-wide DAG hypothesis
is used or proposed as a language restriction.

`transparent_type` derives preservation of the exact type along each transparent
edge by node-typing inversion. `observation_typed` transports typing through the
finite observation. `terminal_canonical` then inverts only actual terminal
constructors. `reference_canonical` combines these results. `no_bottom_reference`
follows because no terminal constructor introduces bottom. It does not claim
that computations cannot have bottom type or that recursive computation terminates.

## Allocation and application to the parent

`allocate g fresh` injects old names with `Sum.inl` and fresh names with `Sum.inr`.
It maps references inside old nodes without changing their content; the old
subgraph gains no edge to a fresh node. `joinTy` preserves every old assignment
exactly. `fresh_no_collision` derives disjointness of old and new names.
`node_map`, `allocation_old_node`, `allocation_old_type` and
`allocation_observation` provide typing/content/observation preservation under
this explicit renaming. No mutable cell update is modeled.

All fresh names are available simultaneously to all fresh nodes. `allocate_typed`
requires individual fresh-node derivations against the joined assignment and
constructs the whole resulting graph typing. It does not assume post-graph
welltypedness. Lambda body typing checks its actual Term, and delay body typing
likewise checks the body. The arbitrary-node premise is still a premise: no
claim is made that paper/source rec constructors already supply those derivations.

`allocate_guard` constructs the post-graph ranks. Old rank stays rank_old; fresh
rank becomes ceiling_old + rank_fresh. An old edge stays old. A fresh-to-old
edge decreases because every old rank is below ceiling_old. A fresh-to-fresh
transparent edge decreases by the local rec rank check. The resulting ceiling is
ceiling_old + ceiling_fresh. Thus the post-graph guard is derived rather than
assumed, and mutually referring fresh guarded nodes need no allocation order.

`typed_subst` proves simultaneous replacement of reference and variable leaves
by typed Terms by induction on the body typing. `closeBody_typed` replaces all
recursive variables by fresh references in one substitution;
`old_body_weakening` preserves old derivations under the joined assignment.
`rec_extension` consumes all these lemmas and returns post-graph typing, finite
typed canonical observation at every old/new reference, and the typed closed
rec body. This discharges the corresponding restricted research-model implication
in the primary-checked construction; it is a concrete application to the parent proof
step, not closure of the paper or native ENV-GRAPH-1 claim.

## Distinguishing constructions and falsifiers

- `mutualLambda` has two lambdas whose bodies call one another. Both ranks are
  zero. `allocatedMutual` allocates them simultaneously into an empty old graph;
  per-node typing, the combined guard and observations are constructed.
- `sharedPair` has two fields pointing to the same unit node, also with equal
  zero ranks. Sharing and guarded edges are not rejected by a DAG requirement.
- `transparentCycle` consists of a view edge and a roll edge back to its start.
  It has a node-typing assignment with bottom everywhere but has no Guarded
  certificate. Hence graph node typing alone cannot justify bottom exclusion.
- `badFresh` allocates a fresh self-alias with bottom typing. Freshness and every
  individual new-node typing premise hold; `badAllocation_unguarded` rejects the
  resulting graph. The local new transparent-edge guard is essential.
- `no_transparent_self` rejects alias, view, roll or evidence self-loops uniformly;
  `no_transparent_two_cycle` and `no_transparent_cycle` cover mixed/longer loops.
- Replacing an old node's type is excluded by `allocation_old_type`; allocating a
  new name equal to an old one contradicts `fresh_no_collision`.

These are theorem constructions in the candidate, not executed tests and not
observations of actual compiler constructors.

## Remaining owners and mutual TODOs

GVG-CHECK-1 — primary: elaborate the frozen Lean file, inspect its theorem/axiom
boundary, repair only after author STOP, and obtain independent review. Falsifier:
any elaboration failure, admitted proof, forbidden axiom, or quantified conclusion
that fails for the represented constructor domain.

GVG-GUARD-COMPLETE-1 — next graph proof allocation: construct a bounded rank from
an explicit finite graph with no all-transparent directed cycle. Falsifier: a
finite cycle-guarded graph for which the proposed construction fails to assign a
strictly decreasing transparent rank. This direction is currently OPEN.

GVG-FORMS-1 — next full-paper graph proof allocation: add the actual missing
constructors and type-changing roll/view/type-evidence rules, then establish the
correct elimination-specific typed observations. Falsifier: a well-typed guarded
μ/view/type-application graph for which transparent traversal changes the type
without preserving the eliminator evidence. Keep this separate from the local
identity-typed `transparent_type` lemma.

GVG-REC-RHS-1 — full paper syntax owner: derive fresh-node typing from the original
rec RHS derivations under simultaneous binder-aware substitution, including all
lambda/adapter/request binders. Current node_map and Term substitution are usable
sublemmas only in their stated domain. Falsifier: capture or a missing recursive
reference in any represented full-paper RHS constructor.

ENV-GRAPH-1 — Luna/source intake: graph readback and original typing from actual
machine local/global initialization, current cells, Lambda/Callee/ValueEntry and
lookup/extend owners, including preallocation and uninitialized states. This
assignment performs no native audit and makes no native correspondence claim.
The existing constructor-map and native-environment notes are used only to retain
that obligation and ownership, not as evidence of graph realization. No production
implementation TODO is authorized or needed by this independent theory packet.

All original Simple-sub generation, accumulation, propagation, levels, extrusion,
intrusion, generalization and F1/FK1/foreign-continuation quantifiers remain
unchanged and OPEN outside their independently established premises.

## Frozen evidence and resources

`4d2c3b17d0ab8d12606c875638426167ce596492167cecf042eb222436229f55`.
Paper dependency: `a003b56a2f32eed06a2c604ef8aed043d43752cbed0b09028eff7f6efac4886b`.

No historical proof is generalized beyond its premises; no historical failed
construction is revived. This file contains a new candidate construction.

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a
failed proof check. Primary owns bounded elaboration, public signature/axiom
inspection, distinguishing examples, repairs after author STOP and fresh
independent review. Author/coauthor cannot independently certify this candidate.
Only the four exact leased files were created; there are no scratch paths,
background processes, descendants, compiler changes or Git operations.
